messages.content: Calculate the energy (in Joules) absorbed or released during the phase change of 100g of water from liquid to steam at its boiling point.

function.name: thermo_calculate_energy
function.description: Calculate the energy required or released during a phase change using mass, the phase transition temperature and the specific latent heat. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

mass.description: Mass of the substance in grams.

substance.description: The substance which is undergoing phase change, default is 'water'

message.content:
To find the energy involved when 100 g of water turns into steam at its boiling point, you multiply the mass by the latent heat of vaporization:

\[
Q = m \times L_{\text{vap}}
\]

* **Mass** \(m = 100\,\text{g}\)
* **Latent heat of vaporization of water** \(L_{\text{vap}} \approx 2257\,\text{J/g}\) (≈ 2260 J/g is often used as a rounded value)

\[
Q = 100\,\text{g} \times 2257\,\frac{\text{J}}{\text{g}} = 225{,}700\,\text{J}
\]

So approximately **\(2.26 \times 10^5\) J** (or 226 kJ) of energy is absorbed during the conversion of 100 g of liquid water to steam at 100 °C.
